notes: An ancient, self-contained civilizational core predating every empire that has since claimed it — earliest attested Christianization 4th century CE (frameworks survey §1). ⚠️ Adjara carries a distinct hatch marker within this region: ethnically Georgian, but with a real, historically-documented Muslim-Georgian religious minority (Ottoman-era legacy, not further researched this pass) — a religious rather than ethnic distinction, kept inside the Kartvelian core rather than split out as its own region, unlike Abkhazia/South Ossetia below.

⚠️ Kept as its own distinctly-colored region, NOT folded into the Georgia/Kartvelian core — Abkhaz is a genuinely separate Northwest Caucasian ethnolinguistic group, not a Georgian sub-identity, the same logic that kept Karakalpakstan separate from the Uzbek Oasis Civilization in the companion Central Asia package. De facto independent, Russian-garrisoned and Russian-recognized since 2008; almost the entire rest of the world still regards it as Georgian territory (frameworks survey §2.2). DISPUTED, NOT RESOLVED — this project's 'research proposes, author disposes' rule applies in full, the same posture as Kirkuk and Israel/Palestine elsewhere in this project.

tier1_group: Iranic/Indo-European (Ossetian — distinct from both Kartvelian and Armenian)
notes: ⚠️ Kept as its own distinctly-colored region for the same ethnic-distinctness reason as Abkhazia above — Ossetian is actually an Iranic/Indo-European language, genuinely unrelated to Kartvelian Georgian, despite sitting inside Georgia's own pre-1990 administrative boundaries. De facto independent and Russian-garrisoned/recognized since the 2008 war. Carries a real formal-status asymmetry with Abkhazia worth remembering when drawing: Georgia does not currently recognize it as a constitutional Autonomous Republic the way Abkhazia formally still is (frameworks survey §2.2) — reflected in a distinguishable hatch/pattern from Abkhazia's own contested treatment, not an identical one. DISPUTED, NOT RESOLVED, same posture as Abkhazia.

Also connects to that package's own S3 Pan-Turkic sphere as new territory — see spheres.csv S1.
